newsitem.title: GERMANY: German thugs jailed for racist attack on Italians.
newsitem.headline: German thugs jailed for racist attack on Italians.

text.p: A German court on Wednesday sentenced two young thugs to 15 and eight-year jail terms for a brutal racist attack on Italian building workers which left one of the victims paralysed and barely able to speak.

The court in Potsdam near Berlin found both men guilty of attempted murder for attacking the Italians with a baseball bat in the town of Trebbin last September after setting out on what the presiding judge called a "real manhunt."

Judge Klaus Przybilla said the assault had been carried out with "an extreme degree of brutality and racial hatred" and that the ruling was intended as a signal against growing violence and hostility towards foreigners.
Germany has tried hard to clamp down on racist and neo-Nazi groups since a three-year wave of anti-foreigner attacks after unification in 1990, in which more than 30 people died.

But the east German state of Brandenburg, which surrounds Berlin, remains a focus for young, shaven-headed right-wingers, or skinheads, who have carried out dozens of attacks on foreigners, vagrants and left-wing groups in the last few years.
In one of the most widely reported incidents, a gang of young skinheads attacked a black member of an American Olympic luge team in eastern Germany in 1993.
A number of skinheads turned up in Potsdam to hear the verdict. Przybilla said the thugs kept looking for new groups of victims.
"We, the judges, believe this has to stop," he said.
He said the two men had set out with the aim of beating the Italians up.
One of the accused, 22-year-old Jan Weicht, clubbed one of the Italians with a baseball bat, leaving him paralysed and only partly able to speak.

The other defendant, aged 20, who received an eight-year sentence as a juvenile, kicked a second Italian and threatened him by holding a blank cartridge pistol to his neck. The victim suffered a broken nose and several broken ribs.
Both the accused had said they acted in self-defence. Their lawyers said they would appeal.
